summary:
We developed a wearable ultrasonic sleep-support system designed to help astronauts improve sleep quality in challenging space environments. The system combines ultrasonic stimulation, machine learning, and embedded hardware to provide personalized sleep-support settings. Before each session, astronauts complete a short questionnaire, and an ML model analyzes their responses and previous session feedback to recommend optimal stimulation parameters, including frequency, amplitude, waveform, and duration. 

These settings are transmitted through a web-based dashboard to an ESP32 microcontroller, which controls the ultrasonic transducers integrated into wearable headgear. After each session, astronaut feedback helps the model improve future recommendations. By combining adaptive personalization with a wearable, non-pharmacological approach, our project aims to address sleep challenges during space missions, where sleep quality is essential for cognitive performance, crew well-being, and mission safety.
details:
Project Details

Our project is a wearable ultrasonic sleep-support system designed to explore personalized sleep stimulation for astronauts living and working in challenging space environments.

How It Works

The system follows a simple adaptive workflow:

  1. Pre-Sleep Assessment: The astronaut completes a short questionnaire describing their current condition and sleep-related factors.
  2. AI-Powered Personalization: A machine learning model analyzes the astronaut's responses alongside feedback from previous sessions. It recommends four key stimulation parameters: frequency, amplitude, waveform, and duration. Instead of relying on fixed settings, the model aims to personalize recommendations and improve them as more feedback becomes available.
  3. Hardware Control: The recommended parameters are transmitted through our web application and backend to an ESP32 microcontroller. The ESP32 controls the ultrasonic signal-generation circuitry and the transducers integrated into wearable headgear.
  4. Post-Session Feedback: After each session, the astronaut provides feedback about their experience. This information is stored and incorporated into future model recommendations, creating a continuous personalization cycle.

Technology and Development Tools

We developed the system using a combination of software, machine learning, and embedded hardware:

  • Python: Core programming language for the backend and machine learning.
  • Scikit-learn: Machine learning model development and personalization.
  • FastAPI: Backend API for handling questionnaire data, predictions, and system communication.
  • Web Technologies: Interactive dashboard for questionnaires, recommendations, and session monitoring.
  • ESP32: Microcontroller responsible for hardware control.
  • Ultrasonic Transducers: Components integrated into wearable headgear to deliver controlled ultrasonic signals.
  • Electronic Signal Generation and Driving Circuitry: Supporting electronics for controlling the stimulation parameters.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The system aims to provide astronauts with a personalized, wearable, and potentially non-pharmacological approach to sleep support. Its main benefits include:

  • Personalized stimulation settings instead of a one-size-fits-all solution.
  • Continuous adaptation based on individual feedback.
  • Integration of machine learning with real-world embedded hardware.
  • A compact system designed with the practical constraints of space environments in mind.
  • Potential to support astronaut well-being, cognitive performance, and mission readiness through better sleep management.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of our project is the integration of ultrasonic stimulation with a feedback-driven machine learning system. Rather than simply generating fixed ultrasonic signals, our approach introduces an adaptive personalization layer that adjusts stimulation recommendations according to individual responses and previous experiences.

Combining a wearable device, intelligent software, and hardware control creates a complete system in which data-driven recommendations can directly influence physical device behavior.

Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered several important factors:

  • Personalization: Different astronauts may respond differently to stimulation, making individual feedback important.
  • Simplicity: We aimed to keep the system architecture straightforward and avoid unnecessary complexity.
  • Wearability: The device should be compact, comfortable, and suitable for use before sleep.
  • Control and Adaptability: Frequency, amplitude, waveform, and duration should be independently adjustable.
  • Space Constraints: Power consumption, hardware size, reliability, and ease of operation are important considerations for space applications.
  • Scientific Validation and Safety: Ultrasonic stimulation parameters and their potential effects on sleep require controlled testing and safety evaluation before any claims of effectiveness can be made.

Our current objective is to integrate the hardware and software into a functional MVP and conduct controlled experiments to evaluate system performance and investigate the relationship between ultrasonic stimulation parameters and sleep-related outcomes.
